title.narrative: UNFPA - stöd till landprogram i DRK

description.narrative:
Denna insats syftar till att förstärka UNFPA: s kapacitet att leverera de resultat som anges i organisationens landprogram för Demokratiska Republiken Kongo under perioden 2020-2023.
I DRK är alla indikatorer som rör kvinnors hälsa, sexuella och reproduktiva tjänster och rättigheter (SRHR) oroande, framförallt är den knappa tillgången till preventivmedel och det höga antalet ungdomsgraviditeter alarmerande. Dessutom är den övergripande policymiljön när det gäller SRHR och befolkningsdynamik inte anpassad till landets utmaningar. UNFPA är en nyckelaktör i DRK, vars starka insatser inom ramen för dess globala mandat behövs för att stödja både beslutsfattare, genomförande aktörer på internationell och nationell nivå, och kunna nå ut till olika målgrupper som kvinnor, ungdomar, vårdgivare och institutioner.
Detta institutionella stöd till UNFPA ger dem flexibilitet, frihet och medel för att positionera sig och ge stöd till aktörer inom SRHR och relaterade frågor i landet.

This contribution aims at strenthening UNFPA's capacity to deliver on the results set by the organisation's country programme for DRC covering the period 2020-2023.
In DRC, all indicators concerning maternal health, sexual and reproductive services and rights (SRHR), including poor access to contraceptives are alarming. Also, overall policy environment with regards to SRHR and population dynamics is inadapted to country's challenges. UNFPA is a key actor in DRC whose strong action within the framework of its global mandate is needed to support both decision makers, implementing actors (international and national), and different target groups (professionals as well as services users, such as the youth).
This contribution proposes providing an institutional support to UNFPA in the country to allow them flexibility, freedom and means to position themselves and provide the needed assistance to the multitude of actors on SRHR and related issues in the country.

This contribution is intended to support the UNFPA DRC country office in contributing to the following objectives: (1) strengthened national capacities to improve financing and develop and implement policies and programmes that address sexual and reproductive health and right’s needs; (2) integrated high quality services delivery and information for maternal health, family planning, Sexually Transmitted Infections/HIV, (3) to ensure that young people and adolescents, especially disadvantaged adolescent’s girls are empowered to have the capacity to claim their rights and access to sexual and reproductive health services; (4) to strengthened national accountability mechanisms to prevent SGBV and promote gender equality and to provide holistic care to victims of SGBV. These objectives will be pursued in stable as well as in humanitarian context.
In addition to the aformentioned objectives it has been decided to provide additional support to UNFPA, as the global champion on Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) and as the lead agency of the Task Force on SEA allegations in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), to strengthen safeguarding mechanisms including prevention, response, coordination and community engagement with regards to PSEA.

sector.narrative: Ending violence against women and girls

description.narrative:
The report reflects a well-structured, multisectoral approach in line with UNFPAs global priorities. The strategic focus on fragility, localization, and innovation is aligned with Sida's commitments to rights-based and sustainable programming.
Results:
1. Reducing Preventable Maternal Deaths - 95% of deliveries in UNFPA supported health facilities were attended by qualified personnel. - 509,760 unsafe abortions and 6,396 maternal deaths were averted. - 1,006 obstetric fistula repairs conducted, with services expanded to 23 of 26 provinces. - Emergency Reproductive Health Services provided in crisis affected areas via mobile clinics and SONU trained providers.
2. Expanding Access to Family Planning - 3.2 million users of modern contraceptives reached. - Evaluation of the supply chain led to clear operational recommendations and support to last mile providers such as Tulane. - Mobile clinics expanded to fragile areas (over 10 clinics established in conflict provinces) - 4.9 million out of school adolescents received vocational starter kits with integrated SRHR education.
3. Addressing Gender-Based Violence (GBV)
- 1,372 GBV survivors received holistic care. - More than 1 million individuals reached through GBV risk awareness and mitigation campaigns. - 3,434 GBV allegations received via green line, including 478 SEA cases in schools. - The Makala prison crisis response was rapid, with provision of post rape kits and dignity supplies.
4. Youth Leadership and Empowerment
- A total of 242,629 out of school girls received entrepreneurship and SRHR education. - CEICA Boma center was revitalized to support youth friendly services and engagement. - Fun activities (e.g., sports broadcasts) were used innovatively to attract youth to services.
5. Policy, Data, and Demographic Intelligence
- Completion of EDSIII (Demographic and Health Survey), with a formal report expected in early 2025. - Strengthening of the National Institute of Statistics and ongoing support to the civil registration system. - Support to the draft statistical law and participation in the ICPD30 review.
Key achievements: - Strong Alignment with UNFPA Strategic Priorities: Clear focus on the three transformative results ending preventable maternal deaths, unmet need for family planning and GBV. - Improving access in Fragile, Hard to Reach Areas: Mobile clinics and decentralized offices (Goma, Lubumbashi, Kinshasa) were instrumental in reaching IDPs and conflict affected populations. - Holistic GBV Programming: Integrated approach with legal, medical, psychosocial, and economic reintegration components. - Youth focused Innovations: Attention to adolescent girls and integration of education, vocational training, and SRHR information is commendable.
Critical reflections (OBS! the analysis below is based on the assumption that the data for 2023 & 2024, cover only the respective years, and do not represent cumulative data)
- UNFPA scaled-up service coverage and maternal death prevention in 2024 compared to 2023 i.e. deliveries in supported facilities attended by qualified staff increased from 90.5% to 95%; deliveries attended by qualified staff increased from from 38,760 in 2023 to 1,308,216 in 2024; averted maternal death almost doubled from 3,056 in 2023 to 6,396 in 2024. - The report indicates a shift from institutional strengthening (2023) to direct service delivery and mobile outreach in crisis settings (2024). - UNFPA seems to have strengthened alignment with H6 partnership, and community based maternal care models.
- Significant changes in GBV programming whereby reduction in scale was replaced by in depth focus with more emphasis on holistic care and institutional reform e.g. a total of 21,372 survivors received care in 2024 compared to 209,600 in 2023 (OBS!2023 figure includes all types of services) - Similarly, the year 2023 focused more on systems-building (FONAREV, PSEA networks) while 2024 focused on incident response, survivor-centered care, and community-level awareness. This change could could be ascribed to the conflict which necessitated the need to focus on incident reporting, survivor-centred care etc. given the increased cases of GBV as a result of the conflict in the East. - Cross-Cutting Themes and Fragility Context; UNFPA maintained strong presence in Eastern DRC conflict zones via decentralized offices (Goma, Lubumbashi). - Services provided in more than 15 provinces with mobile clinics, particularly North Kivu, Ituri, Tanganyika. - The year 2024, saw increased focus on SEA prevention, positive masculinity, and community based GBV referral systems.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
